lab_ocr_unavailable.description: Workflow #396 LAB-3: an OCR evaluation of actinglab or the Lab cannot run because the offline tool loaded no usable OCR model. The offline tools load the OCR provider the Runtime uses (the in-process ppocr-ctc engine over the model folders of the vision root that the Runtime configuration's vision section names, always on the CPU). A command that would evaluate an OCR target refuses with this code (exit 3) and names the target as target_id; a Lab mark self-test, the first decision of record stop and the capabilities report give it as their reason. path is the vision root when it is known. Its caused_by link says why: lab_ocr_vision_unconfigured, a configuration read or decode code, vision_root_unavailable, vision_models_empty, lab_ocr_model_missing or lab_ocr_runtime_missing.
lab_ocr_unavailable.common_causes: actinglab runs outside an installation or a single-location root, the configuration has no vision section, or the vision root holds no OCR model folder. A Lab recording step whose click follows a located-text mark needs the model at every record mark of the step, since the click's box comes from the OCR, and record stop's first decision needs it when step 1's guard is a located text.
lab_ocr_unavailable.handling: Install the OCR model folder and ONNX Runtime under the Runtime's vision root and run actinglab from the installation's tools (or runtime) folder; mark a step that follows a located-text mark only with the OCR model available.

lab_ocr_vision_unconfigured.description: Workflow #396 LAB-3, a cause of lab_ocr_unavailable: the offline tool has no Runtime configuration with a vision section. It does not run from an installation or a single-location root, or the selected configuration has no vision section.
lab_ocr_vision_unconfigured.common_causes: actinglab was started from a copy outside the installation, or the Runtime configuration has no vision section.
lab_ocr_vision_unconfigured.handling: Run actinglab from the installation's tools folder, or add the vision section to the Runtime configuration.

lab_ocr_model_missing.description: Workflow #396 LAB-3, a cause of lab_ocr_unavailable: the vision root's models folder (path) holds model folders, but none is an OCR model.

lab_ocr_runtime_missing.description: Workflow #396 LAB-3, a cause of lab_ocr_unavailable: the vision root has no usable ONNX Runtime library at path (ort\onnxruntime.dll). Its caused_by link is the OS failure when the OS reported one.

record_click_follow_invalid.description: Workflow #396 REC-4: a click of a Lab recording step that follows a template mark (record mark --click-follow, a request's click.follow), or (#463 L2) a located-text mark, does not hold; mark_id is the followed mark and follow_problem says why. A declaration that cannot hold (not_template, not_required, guard_conflict, and for a located-text mark page_needs_followed_text) refuses record mark with this code (exit 3) and nothing is written. A frame of the step on which the click does not hold (primary_mismatch or press_outside_found_box on the primary frame, template_unmatched or click_outside_frame on any live frame) is a refused mark's reason inside record_mark_rejected, with the frame; a press_outside_found_box of a request that declares the mark again lists as differing_members the members besides the names that it changed (#463 L2 fix 2). The stage is record_click_follow_check.
record_click_follow_invalid.common_causes: The click follows a color, check or value-test mark, an OCR mark that declares no locate, a template or located-text mark that only an any_of check names, or another guard was named; a followed located-text mark is the step's only mark, or a check of the step names it, so the page would need the name; the template matches elsewhere on the primary frame, is not found on a sample frame, or the followed click box leaves a sample frame; after the step's click was executed, the located-text mark was declared again with a member besides its names changed (another region, other cells, another locate, languages, match_mode, minimum_confidence, unique or any other member; differing_members names them), and the press lies outside the box it gives on the primary frame.
record_click_follow_invalid.handling: Follow a required template mark of the step, or a located-text mark (an OCR mark with locate), and let it be the guard; give a step whose click follows a located-text mark another mark that tells this screen from the other screens of the task, for example a template of its title or of a fixed element (a mark that also holds on the next screen does not help), and keep the located text out of its checks; crop the template so that its best match on the primary frame is the crop itself; give it a search area that covers every position it moves to, and a click box that stays inside the frame there; to change only the names of a located-text mark after the press, remove it and add it again in one request with the same id and every other member that the recording holds equal (all but its self_test, created_at_unix_ms and initiator: for a located-text mark its family, region and unique and the OCR members languages, timeout_ms, match_mode, case_sensitive, minimum_confidence, model_ref, model_sha256 and locate), as record status shows the mark in located_text, and only its new expected names; or reopen the step and press again.

record_gesture_execution_unsupported.description: #411 Lab BD: do --capture --record was asked to execute a Lab recording step whose declared gesture a Lab operation cannot press, a single-touch drag with a vertical brake (single_touch_drag_with_vertical_brake_v1); nothing was captured, pressed or recorded (exit 3).
record_gesture_execution_unsupported.common_causes: The open step declares a brake drag; Lab operations press taps, long taps and swipes only, and running one declared operation as the kernel runs it is not available in this version.
record_gesture_execution_unsupported.handling: Reach the screen after the gesture by other means (for example a lab run of a package that performs it), then close the step with record mark --close-step or give its next frame offline; the generated package still declares the gesture.

record_archive_target_not_empty.description: Workflow #449 REC-ARCH: record archive --copy-to names a directory that exists and is not empty, or a path that is no directory; nothing was written and the recording is as it was (exit 3; actinglab details path and reason, not_empty or not_a_directory).
record_archive_target_not_empty.common_causes: The copy target is an earlier copy, a directory holding other files, or a file.
record_archive_target_not_empty.handling: Give a directory that does not exist yet or is empty; the copy never merges into or overwrites anything.

record_archive_verify_failed.description: Workflow #449 REC-ARCH: a file an archive's manifest lists does not hold the sha256 the manifest gives, or cannot be read: a copy record archive --copy-to made (checked copy), or a file of the recording's own directory when an archived recording is named again with --record-id (checked recording). Nothing is deleted, what was copied stays, and the recording stays archived (exit 5; actinglab details file, path, checked, reason sha256_mismatch or unreadable, every failure in failures, the files copied in copied; on a copy also record_id, archived and manifest).
record_archive_verify_failed.common_causes: A stored frame or the step table was changed or damaged after it was recorded, or the copy target's disk failed.
record_archive_verify_failed.handling: Read the file it names. Put the recorded file back or copy again into another empty directory with record archive --record-id <id> --copy-to <dir>; no second manifest is written.

record_not_archived.description: Workflow #449 REC-ARCH: the recording record archive --record-id or record reopen names is not an archived recording of the instance; nothing was written (exit 3; actinglab details record_id and state: missing, active, stopped, unarchived, or the session header's status).
record_not_archived.common_causes: The id names no recording of the state directory, the instance's active recording (reopen), a stopped recording, or a recording left behind by record start --force that was never archived.
record_not_archived.handling: Run record status for the instance's recording; archive the active one with record archive, and reopen only one an archive ended.

record_select_invalid.description: #463 R1: the select of a Lab recording step (a request's select, the choice in a list of fixed slots by the name read in each slot) cannot be declared, or record stop cannot generate it; select_problem says why. record mark is refused (exit 3) and nothing is written; record stop refuses the same way and writes nothing. with_follow, with_gesture, with_click, with_retry, on_optional_step and with_application name what the step or the request declares beside the select (with_application also a select on an application step, which has no frame); on_final_step a select on the last step of a stopped recording; slot_outside_frame a slot outside the frame; name_id_invalid a name's id, wanted_name_invalid the wanted value's name, name_duplicate, default_not_in_names, pressed_not_in_names, wanted_name_taken, on_empty_key_invalid, on_empty_key_reserved (the task's own <task_id>_done key) and on_empty_key_taken (another select step's key) a name or key; guard_missing a page without a guard; kernel_refused the kernel's admission of the select step as record stop would generate it, its code in loader_code (a bound of the read that only the kernel checks, such as a timeout above its limit); no_select a clear_select on a step that has no select (#463 R2); on_empty_key_of_ending an on_empty key that is the outcome key of an ending of the recording (#463 R2 fix 1, a select declared after the ending); choice_not_refined (#463 S2-6, record stop and its dry run only, and the code of record ready's item select_unrefined) a step marked as holding a choice (a request's choice) that no select refines yet, so its package would know no names; no_choice (#463 S2-6 fix round 1) a request's choice false on a step that is not marked as holding a choice, so there is nothing to take off; drop_of_choice (#463 stage two, train, fix round) a drop_step of a step that holds a choice (marked as holding one, or refined by a select), the last step too, since its press may have chosen the item already selected, which changes nothing on the screen and still matters to a run handed another value; transition_of_choice (the same round) a to_transition of a step that holds a choice, which a page transition would lose (actinglab details step, and loader_code and detail for kernel_refused). A step marked as holding a choice keeps the rules a select step keeps, with the same words.
record_select_invalid.common_causes: The request also declares a click, a click follow, a gesture, a retry, an optional step or an application operation, or names an application step; the step's page has only OCR marks, so it gives no guard; a name or the wanted value breaks the parameter grammar, or the default or the pressed name is not one of the names; another select step of the recording uses the same wanted name or on_empty key, or the on_empty key is the task's _done key (a second select that leaves on_empty_key out takes the first one's default), or an ending's key; the select is marked on the last step of a stopped recording; a read the kernel's admission refuses; a choice marked on a step and not refined by a select before record stop; choice false sent for a step that carries no mark; drop_step or to_transition sent for a step marked as holding a choice or refined by a select.
record_select_invalid.handling: Send the select alone as the step's effect, without click, retry, optional or application, on a step with a frame; give the step's page a template, color, color digest or check mark that recognizes it; use names, a wanted name and an on_empty key of their grammars, distinct across the recording and from its endings' keys (give a second select its own on_empty_key), with the default and the pressed name among the names; mark the select on a step before the last one; for kernel_refused read loader_code and detail and change the read. For choice_not_refined run record ready, which lists every such step (select_unrefined), and refine each with record mark --step <n> and its select, on the active or the stopped recording, or take its mark off with choice false; then run record stop again. For no_choice there is nothing to do: the step carries no mark (record status shows each step's choice). For drop_of_choice and transition_of_choice withdraw the choice first, with choice false where the step carries the mark and clear_select where a select refines it, then drop or convert the step again.

record_ending_invalid.description: #463 R2: an ending of a Lab recording (record mark --ending or a request's ending, a screen that ends the business another way after the last press, taken from a frame; or record mark --remove-ending, a request's remove_ending) cannot be taken or given up, or record stop cannot generate it; ending_problem says why. record mark is refused (exit 3) and nothing is written; record stop refuses the same way and writes nothing. recording_active an ending on an active recording; with_other_change a step change beside ending or remove_ending, or both; key_invalid, key_reserved (the task's own <task_id>_done key), key_of_select (a select step's on_empty key, checked again at record stop), key_exists (another ending's) and key_unknown (remove_ending naming no ending) the outcome key; page_exists another ending's page name; no_marks an ending without a mark; ocr_alone_unchecked (fix 1, record stop's self-check item 9 only) an ending whose page rests on OCR marks alone, which the Lab, without an OCR model, could not check against a screen the run may show instead (actinglab details outcome_key; for ocr_alone_unchecked also page, against, frames and step or other_outcome_key).
record_ending_invalid.common_causes: The recording was not stopped yet; the request also names a step, a frame of a step, marks of a step or another change; the key is the usual ending's, a select step's on_empty key or another ending's, or breaks its grammar; remove_ending names a key with a typo; the ending names no mark; the ending was taken with OCR marks only and record stop runs where the Lab has no OCR model.
record_ending_invalid.handling: Run record stop first and take the ending on the stopped recording, alone in its request; give the ending its own key of the grammar ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_]{0,127}$, its own page name, and at least one mark that recognizes its screen; read record status for the endings the recording holds. For ocr_alone_unchecked run record stop where the Lab has its OCR model, or give up the ending with record mark --remove-ending <key> and take it again with a mark that is not OCR, such as a template of its message.

record_ending_ambiguous.description: #463 R2: record stop's self-check item 9 found an ending's page passing on recorded frames of a screen the run may show instead of it, where the run, which evaluates the endings before the usual ending, would end on the ending; against says which: previous the frames of a step after whose press the run awaits the endings (its page, or its page transition's frames when it has one: the screen before the result of that press showed), usual the frames of the last step, other_ending the frames of another ending. Nothing is written (exit 3; actinglab details outcome_key, page, frames, and step or other_outcome_key).
record_ending_ambiguous.common_causes: The ending's marks hold on the screen before the last press, on the usual ending's screen or on another ending's screen too: a mark reused from a step, a color of a background the screens share, or a template that is no part of the ending's own message.
record_ending_ambiguous.handling: Give up the ending with record mark --remove-ending <key> and take it again with a mark that holds on its screen only, such as a template of its message or a button; check with record stop --dry-run.

record_optional_after_invalid.description: #463 R4: an optional step a stopped Lab recording inserts after the effect of one of its steps (record mark --optional-after <k> or a request's optional_after: a pop-up after which the path goes on, taken from a frame), or gives up again (record mark --remove-inserted <n>, a request's remove_inserted), cannot be inserted or given up; optional_after_problem says why. record mark is refused (exit 3) and nothing is written. recording_active a step inserted on an active recording; with_other_change another change beside optional_after or remove_inserted, or both; step_unknown, step_last and step_application the step k names: none (or a dropped or converted one), the last step, a step whose effect is an application operation; no_marks an inserted step without a mark; no_effect (#463 KR-1, 0.12.70, in place of no_click) one without an effect, neither a click nor a key; clears_optional a request that clears optional on an inserted step; not_inserted remove_inserted naming no inserted step that is not given up yet (actinglab details step, and members for with_other_change).
record_optional_after_invalid.common_causes: The recording was not stopped yet; the request also names a step, a frame, marks of a step, an ending or another change; k names a step that is not there, the last step (nothing is pressed after it) or an application step; the pop-up's request gives no mark, or neither a click nor a key; --not-optional names an inserted step; --remove-inserted names a recorded step or a step given up already.
record_optional_after_invalid.handling: Run record stop first and insert the pop-up on the stopped recording, alone in its request: --optional-after <k> with the step after whose press the run met it, --frame of the pop-up (the pinned frame of the run, as material writes it), a mark of the pop-up's own (such as a template of its title) and the click that closes it; read record status for the steps in the order they run; give up an inserted step with record mark --remove-inserted <n>, its own serial number. Then run record stop, which checks it as every optional step.

lab_scene_size_unsupported.description: Workflow #392 DA-5cd: an offline scene, a stored image (recognize, detect-page, current-page, is-visible, offline observe, do --dry-run, ensure --dry-run and wait on saved scenes, tap-target --dry-run, navigate --dry-run), cannot be brought to its package's coordinate_space (its base), so nothing is evaluated (exit 2; actinglab's own line, and serve --stdio --front mcp, exit 1 for every refusal). The train of DA-5 (Workflow #392 DA-5ab and DA-5cd): a stored image is judged, reduced and answered as the Lab's live observation takes a frame of its size, by the same function (the kernel's frame gate for a Lab frame); this code is the stored image's refusal of that function, as display_map_unresolved is a live capture's, and neither answers for the other's cause. frame_width and frame_height are the scene's size, base_width and base_height the package's coordinate_space, and display_problem the frame gate's word for why: layout_undeclared another ratio, scale_below_base a scene smaller than the package, orientation_mismatch the package's other orientation. A scene of the coordinate_space is evaluated as before; one of its ratio, not smaller and in its orientation (5/4 of it too) is reduced to it as the live observation reduces a frame, and its answer names frame_coordinates in the base form (space base, base_pixels, reduced_from, orientation, applies_to). Before this code such a scene was refused validation_failed.
lab_scene_size_unsupported.common_causes: The scene was captured on an instance whose display has another ratio than the package or is smaller than the package; or the scene was cropped or turned.
lab_scene_size_unsupported.handling: Give a scene of the package's coordinate_space or of its ratio, at least as large and in its orientation (1600x900, 1920x1080, 2560x1440, 3840x2160 for 1280x720), uncropped; or set the instance's display to such a size and capture again.

record_display_not_base.description: Workflow #392 DA-5cd: this instance's display is not the base size, so nothing was recorded. A Lab recording is made at the base size (STANDARD_PACK_BASE_SIZE, 1280x720, the coordinate_space every standard package declares). record start refuses an instance whose display the Runtime last observed (its display.frame_extent fact, the first frame of the latest contained task run on it) at another size, before anything is written and before anything is asked of the scheduling, so the instance is not held; that is an early warning (fix round 1): record start writes the base size in the recording's header (base_size), and the first frame that enters the recording is checked against it before it is stored: a frame of another size (another aspect, smaller or larger, whether or not the Runtime knew the display) is refused with nothing written, no frame, no step and the header as it was, and the recording stays active as it was. The train of DA-5 (Workflow #392 DA-5ab and DA-5cd): every path that records judges the frame it took as such a first frame before anything is sent or written, whether or not it will store it: tap, swipe and long-tap --record, do --capture --record (one frame captured through the Runtime before its press) and observe --capture --record (the Runtime's frame, after it observed). The train's fix round 1: on the paths that press (tap, swipe and long-tap --record, session app --record), a frame that would be the recording's first is judged before it is stored as if the recording already had its size, by the judgement record stop makes, so that a recording whose header names no base size is refused here a first frame of a larger display of the base size's ratio, before anything is sent. frame_width and frame_height are the display's size (the frame's at the first frame), base_width and base_height the base size (exit 3; actinglab's own line, and serve --stdio --front mcp, exit 1 for every refusal; actinglab details display and base, each {width, height}).
record_display_not_base.common_causes: The instance's display is 1920x1080, 3840x2160, a handset's 2400x1080, a portrait display or another size than 1280x720; at record start, the display was set back to 1280x720 but no task has run on the instance since (an instance whose scheduling is paused runs none), so the Runtime still knows the earlier display.
record_display_not_base.handling: Record on an instance whose display is the base size: set this instance's display to 1280x720, or use another instance at that size. When record start refused a display that was set back since, the Runtime observes it only when a task runs on the instance: resume its scheduling until a task has run, then start again, or start on another instance at the base size. After a refused first frame the recording is as it was: take the frame again once the display is the base size.

record_size_not_base.description: Workflow #392 DA-5cd fix round 1: this recording holds frames that are not the base size: a recording whose header names a base size (base_size, written by record start) and whose frames are of any other size, or one whose header names none (started before fix round 1) and whose frames show a larger display of the base size's ratio (a pure scale the display adapter maps onto it, such as 1920x1080 or 3840x2160). record stop (its dry run and the regeneration of a stopped recording marked again too) refuses it before anything is planned or written, the recording and its session staying active and the hold kept, and converts nothing; record ready lists it first as missing size_not_base and runs no self-check; a frame added to it (a recorded step's, a sample's, a transition's, an ending's) is refused before it is stored. The train of DA-5 (Workflow #392 DA-5ab and DA-5cd): every recorded step asks this judgement before it sends anything, and nothing is captured, sent or written: tap, swipe and long-tap --record and session app --record before they capture (also when the open step is marked and the frame before the press would not be stored), do --capture --record before its press, observe --capture --record before its capture. frame_width and frame_height are the recording's frames' size, base_width and base_height the base size (exit 3; actinglab's own line, and serve --stdio --front mcp, exit 1 for every refusal; actinglab details frames and base, each {width, height}).
record_size_not_base.common_causes: A recording made on a display that is not the base size before this release, or a recording file changed by hand.
record_size_not_base.handling: Archive the recording with record archive (record status, record frames and record archive read it as before) and record the task again on an instance whose display is the base size, 1280x720.

record_frame_unknown.description: #463 S2-7: a page transition of record mark (a request's transition with frame_id or sample_frame_ids, the request form only) names by its frame id a frame this Lab recording does not hold: no frame of a step (superseded frames included), of a step's page transition or of an ending has that id. Nothing is written (exit 3; actinglab's own line, and serve --stdio --front mcp, exit 1 for every refusal; actinglab details step and frame_id). A frame the recording holds whose stored file no longer holds its sha256 is record_frame_hash_mismatch, as every stored frame read back.
record_frame_unknown.common_causes: The id was mistyped, taken from another recording, or read from a record frames or record status answer of another recording.
record_frame_unknown.handling: Read the recording's frames with record status or record frames --step <k> (the frames before and after a press, with their ids) and name one of them, or give the frame as a PNG file with frame.

record_drop_unproven.description: #463 S2-7: record mark --drop-step (a request's step_action drop_step) names a step before the last effective one, and the frames this Lab recording stored contradict that its press changed nothing, or do not hold what the comparison needs. The tool drops such a step only when its stored frames do not contradict that its press changed nothing; whether a press mattered is the agent's judgement, the tool refuses only what the frames contradict. drop_problem says why: frames_not_recorded (no press on record with the stored frame it was sent on and the stored frame after it, as tap, swipe and long-tap --record record one, or a frame the comparison needs is not on record), screen_changed (the frame after the press differs from the frame before it) or next_screen_differs (the next step's frame before its press differs from the frame before this press). Fix round 1: two frames are the same screen when two comparisons hold, both by the measure and bound stage one calls a screen still by (frame_change_milli at most FRAME_CHANGE_MAX_MILLI, 1500): the whole frame, and the neighbourhood of the press (its rectangle, a point a rectangle of one pixel and a swipe the rectangle spanned by its two ends, grown on every side by one cell of the whole-frame grid at the recording's size and clamped to the frame); drop_comparison names the one that showed the change, frame or press_region (the whole frame is compared first). Each comparison averages the colour of 16 by 9 cells of its region and sees a change only when it adds up to more than 1.5 of the measure's 93 points a cell on average: a change confined to two cells is never seen; over the whole frame at 1280x720 a cell is 80 by 80 pixels, so a small change away from the press (a counter, a badge or a switch elsewhere) is not seen. Nothing is written (exit 3; actinglab's own line, and serve --stdio --front mcp, exit 1 for every refusal; actinglab details step, drop_comparison, before_frame, after_frame, next_step, next_before_frame and frame_change_milli, the value of the comparison that showed the change, where they are known). The last effective step is dropped as before, without these comparisons.
record_drop_unproven.common_causes: The press opened something (a pop-up, another page, a change of a value), so its screen after or the next step's screen differs; the press was made by do --capture --record or an application operation, whose frames before and after are not on record; the step is not a press at all.
record_drop_unproven.handling: Leave the step in the package (it does something), or, when the press only seemed to do nothing, read its frames with record frames --step <k>. A step whose press did change something is no press to drop: mark it as any other step.

case_schema_unsupported.description: #463 RC-1 (contracts/resource-regression-case.md): a regression case's case.json declares another schema_version than actingcommand.resource-regression-case.v1, or none. The reader of the Runtime's case contract does not run it: its verdict is not_run, with this warning among the case's warnings and no check, and it fails nothing (resource regression exits 0 for it). schema_version is the one the case declares, when it declares a text of at most 256 bytes without a control character.
case_schema_unsupported.common_causes: The case is of a repository that writes its cases in another format (one case with several frames and its own checks, or rectangles and checks without a schema), run by that repository's own script.
case_schema_unsupported.handling: Nothing to do for a case another script runs. To have the Runtime run it, write it as an actingcommand.resource-regression-case.v1 case (contracts/resource-regression-case.md).

resource_regression_scene_outside_rects.description: #463 RC-1 (contracts/resource-regression-case.md, the scene rule): count pixels of a regression case's scene that lie outside every rectangle of its scene_construction are not the canvas colour (scene_construction.canvas.fill). The case still runs and its verdict does not change for it; the warning is among the case's warnings.
resource_regression_scene_outside_rects.common_causes: A hand-made scene pasted more of the source frame than its rectangles name, or the rectangles do not name every patch; the canvas colour in case.json is not the one the scene was drawn on.
resource_regression_scene_outside_rects.handling: List every pasted patch in scene_construction.rects, or paste only what they name onto a canvas of the fill colour, and update scene_sha256 with the scene's new bytes.

case_member_unknown.description: #463 RC-1 fix round 1 (contracts/resource-regression-case.md, the reader): a member of a regression case's top level that the contract does not name. The top level is open: the reader reads past it and names it once in this warning among the case's warnings, first; the case is read and run as if it were not there and its verdict does not change for it (resource regression exits 0 for it). member is its name, when it is a text of at most 256 bytes without a control character. Inside the parts the runner evaluates (scene_construction, expect, expect.observe, an entry of expect.recognize) an unknown member stays the failure member_unknown.
case_member_unknown.common_causes: The repository writes a member of its own into its cases (a note, a reviewer, a date) that its own runner ignores, or a member of a later version of the format.
case_member_unknown.handling: Nothing to do when the member is the repository's own note. If it was meant as one of the contract's members, correct its name.

record_case_failed.description: #463 S2-10 (contracts/lab-recording.md, Regression cases written with the package): a regression case record stop made from the recording for the package it generated (one per step with a press and a page, on the frame its press was sent on; one for the final screen; one per ending, on the frame it was taken from: a black canvas with, pasted where they are in the frame, the regions every recognition target of the package declares) misses on that package when the one runner of contracts/resource-regression-case.md runs it, its verdict failed: its page is not recognised on its scene (page_mismatch, or page_conflict among pages that are not its own), a target it expects fails (target_mismatch), or another check fails. A page recognised beside another page of the package is no miss (the coordinator's ruling after the first round, R2's ruling 4 as precedent): that case is written without expect.observe and named record_case_page_ambiguous, and only failing in that form is a miss. It is a failure of record stop's last self-check, cases: the case is not written and record stop refuses as at any self-check's failure, nothing written, the recording and the session staying as they were (exit 3; actinglab details case, the case's id, page, as the page detection names it, <game>/<page>, as the case and its warnings do (fix round 3), frame_id, step and artifact_step or outcome_key, verdict, and checks, every failed check as the runner answered it). regression_problem is the word of the first failed check. record ready lists every failing case, each an item of what cases with the case's id and checks in its details; it writes nothing.
record_case_failed.common_causes: A target whose verdict depends on more of the screen than the region the package declares for it (a text-recognition model that reads the whole frame, for one): the scene holds only the declared regions, so the page that passed on the frame is not recognised on the case's scene.
record_case_failed.handling: Run record ready and read each item's checks; give the page a mark that holds within its own region on its screen (a template of a fixed element, a colour of a fixed area), then run record stop again.

record_case_page_ambiguous.description: #463 S2-10, the coordinator's ruling after the first round (R2's ruling 4 as precedent: the usual ending's page passing on an ending's frames is no refusal; contracts/lab-recording.md, Regression cases written with the package): the page a regression case record stop made expects is recognised on its scene, but so is another page of the package (the runner's page_conflict, the case's own page among the pages matched). A linear run waits for each step's own page and never asks which page of the whole package a screen is, so this is no miss: the case is made again without expect.observe, with every recognition target its page requires (passed true) and (fix round 3, the coordinator's ruling) every target its page forbids (passed false), so that it states that this page holds on this scene, run again in that form and written when it passes (failing then is record_case_failed); a forbidden target a scene cannot evaluate (a click-only target, which no page set admits in forbidden today) is left out and named in forbidden_left_out. lab.cases.warnings and record ready's warnings name it: {code, case, page, other_pages, written: true, forbidden_left_out?, message}. Fix round 3, one cause per word: a case not written because it has no target to pin is record_case_ambiguous_not_written, not this. It refuses nothing (exit 0).
record_case_page_ambiguous.common_causes: An earlier step's marks also hold on a later screen (a background the screens share, a button that stays), or an ending's marks beside the usual ending's on one screen; the screens differ only where no mark of the package reads.
record_case_page_ambiguous.handling: Nothing is required. To make the case prove its page too, give the page a mark of its own screen that the other page's screen does not show, or give the other page a forbidden mark (record mark --step <k> --forbid <mark>) that holds on this screen only, and run record stop again.

record_case_bare_canvas.description: #463 S2-10 (contracts/lab-recording.md, Regression cases written with the package): the page a regression case record stop wrote expects is also a page the package's page detection answers on the bare canvas, the black canvas with no patch at all, run once per package; the case proves nothing of its page (its marks pass where nothing was pasted, a dark colour for one). It is written, and lab.cases.warnings names it ({code, case, page, message}); it refuses nothing (exit 0).
record_case_bare_canvas.common_causes: The page's marks are colours of a dark area, or a template of a dark patch, which the black canvas shows too.
record_case_bare_canvas.handling: Nothing is required. To make the case prove its page, give the page a mark of a bright or textured area of its own screen and run record stop again.

record_case_ambiguous_not_written.description: #463 S2-10 fix round 3 (contracts/lab-recording.md, Regression cases written with the package; one cause per word, split from record_case_page_ambiguous): the page a regression case record stop made expects is recognised on its scene beside another page of the package (the runner's page_conflict, the case's own page among the pages matched), and the page has no recognition target to pin (none it requires, none it forbids that a scene can evaluate): without expect.observe the case would declare nothing, so it is not written. lab.cases.warnings and record ready's warnings name it: {code, case, page, other_pages, written: false, message}. It refuses nothing (exit 0). A page set refuses a page that requires no target, so no recording made today reaches it.
record_case_ambiguous_not_written.common_causes: None in a recording made today: a page set refuses a page that requires no target; the word keeps this consequence apart from a case written without the page judgement.
record_case_ambiguous_not_written.handling: Mark a target on that page's screen (record mark on its step) and run record stop again: the case is then written.

record_case_whole_frame.description: #463 S2-10 fix round 3 (contracts/lab-recording.md, Regression cases written with the package): a recognition target of the package reads the whole frame (its region, or a template's search area, is the whole frame, which record mark accepts), so the scene of a regression case record stop wrote, which holds exactly the regions the package's targets read, is the whole frame. Each such case is written and lab.cases.warnings names it ({code, case, page, targets, message}, targets the targets that read the whole frame), so that the agent who chose that region sees it. Nothing is proposed and nothing is refused for it (exit 0).
record_case_whole_frame.common_causes: A mark drawn over the whole screen, or a template searched for anywhere on it.
record_case_whole_frame.handling: Nothing is required. A smaller region or search area of the same target gives scenes of patches.

record_cases_ocr_unavailable.description: #463 S2-10 fix round 3 (contracts/lab-recording.md, Regression cases written with the package): the Lab has no text-recognition model and the package's page detection reads a text target (LabOcr::require_pages refuses), so the runner judged no regression case's page: every case's page check is not_run with ocr_unavailable, and the bare canvas and the ambiguity rule judge nothing. The cases are written without any page judgement and are judged where a model is; record stop says so once, first in lab.cases.warnings ({code, message}), beside the cases not proven. It refuses nothing (exit 0).
record_cases_ocr_unavailable.common_causes: A package with an OCR mark, a located-text mark or a value test, stopped where the Lab finds no text-recognition model.
record_cases_ocr_unavailable.handling: Nothing is required. To have the pages judged, run record stop where the Lab has a text-recognition model, or run the written cases there (resource regression).

record_key_invalid.description: #463 KR-1 (contracts/lab-recording.md, Key steps): a Lab recording step's key, the back key a step presses in place of a click, declared on the recording after the fact and never sent while recording (a request's key {"key": "back"}, record mark --key back, or an inserted optional step's optional_after.key), cannot be declared or generated; key_problem says why. record mark is refused at the request or at the step, and record stop at its pre-check; nothing is written (exit 3; actinglab's own line, and serve --stdio --front mcp, exit 1 for every refusal; actinglab details step, the step named or, for an inserted step, the step it is inserted after, and key for word_unknown). word_unknown the key is no word of the vocabulary, back alone; with_click the request declares a click beside it (a rectangle, a source mark, a followed mark, a gesture or a press box), or an inserted step both a click and a key; with_application an application operation beside it; with_retry a click retry beside it (a key step declares no retry); application_entry the step is the application entry step, which has no frame; application_step the step's effect is an application operation; holds_choice a key and a choice on one step (a select or a choice mark, on the step or in the request); step_not_effective the step is dropped or converted into a page transition; guard_missing (record stop, and record ready's key_guard_missing) a key step names no guard. A second effect without replace_click is not this code: record_step_effect_exists, as for every effect.
record_key_invalid.common_causes: A key word other than back; a key sent in one request with a click, an application operation, a retry, a select or a choice; a key named on the application entry step, an application step, a step that holds a choice or a dropped step; a key step whose guard was never named.
record_key_invalid.handling: Send the key alone with the step (and replace_click where the step has a click); withdraw a choice first; name the key step's guard with record mark --step <k> --click-guard <id>, a template, colour, colour digest, check or value-test mark of its page, then run record ready and record stop.

record_click_follow_check.description: Checking a Lab recording click that follows a template mark (Workflow #396 REC-4) or a located-text mark (#463 L2): its declaration, and the followed mark and its click box on every live frame of the step.
